content.text: Two windows will cover the whole run.

The campaign finished on schedule. It ran from June 7 at 05:00 UTC to June 15 at 05:00 UTC, which is midnight Central on both ends. Nothing is still running.

**Recap**

| | Total |
|---|---|
| Spend | **$666.08** of the $700 budget |
| Impressions | **607,112** |
| Link clicks | **228** |

By post:

| Post | Spend | Impressions | Link clicks |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2195032901022795095 ("Nashville bus stops get brutal…") | $264.33 | 215,201 | 92 |
| 2195214094957680647 ("The whole ask…") | $280.62 | 214,155 | 94 |
| 2195395288890401955 ("Summer heat is here…") | $121.15 | 177,756 | 42 |

**Setup**
- There was one campaign with one ad group, targeting the United States and ages 18 and over. It ran on all X placements with automatic bidding and optimized for link clicks.
- The ad group had an $85 daily cap and a $700 total cap.
- I promoted all three approved posts and wrote no new ones.

**What I saw**
- The first two posts each got a little over 90 link clicks, at about $2.90 per click for the first and $3.00 for the second. The third got 42 clicks at about $2.88 per click. It got fewer clicks mainly because it was served less.
- The posts performed too similarly for a pause or a budget shift to be clearly justified. I made no changes after launch.
- I used a single "18 and over" age target. Splitting it into several age ranges wasn't possible, because the API doesn't offer an exact 25–34 or 50+ option.

**Caveats**
- I can only report clicks to your site. X can't see signatures, so I can't say how many clicks became signups. Please check that count against your own records.
- I didn't spend about $34 of the budget.
